payload.title: Flexible procedure still requires fairness and a valid remedy
payload.core_explanation_md:
The Tribunal framework is guided by natural justice and the Act/rules rather than mechanically importing every CPC procedure. It nevertheless has the described powers to summon witnesses, require records, receive affidavits, review decisions and address default or ex-parte orders. Bank-record evidence must use its applicable evidentiary framework.

The section 20 appeal is separate: its stated thirty days run from receipt of the order copy, with the described consent-order restriction and possible condonation on sufficient cause. Those features should not be confused with a limitation period for the original debt claim. A right to request condonation is not proof that delay has been excused.

self_check.prompt_text: Does not bound by every CPC procedure mean no natural justice?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Statutory procedure and fairness still govern.
